description: Corpora used by the humanization evaluation. Non-owner corpora are read in place from $NOBOTRS_INTERNAL_DIR (default /mnt/storage/projects/nobotrs/docs/internal) and never committed. Only the owner-posts corpus has committed text, approved by the owner on 2026-11-21 (roadmap decision 1). Reports may carry counts, rates, intervals, rule IDs and hashed sample IDs only.

corpora.licence: Owner's own blog posts, already published at kerryhatcher.com. Committed with owner approval (2026-11-21).
corpora.use: Primary owner-corpus comparison: rule lift (Task 3), editor-independent checks, hotspot AUROC (Task 6). Confounded by genre and era; report stratified by genre with the caveat.

corpora.licence: Dataset card: human outputs and prompts CC BY-NC 4.0; model_output under the generating models' terms; human_edits MIT unless model terms apply. Never committed.
corpora.use: Model output vs human output on the same prompts (Task 3 comparison b); editor alignment model_output to human_edits (Task 4); hotspot validity (Task 6). Showing excerpts to readers is open roadmap decision 6.

corpora.licence: Dataset card declares MIT. Never committed.
corpora.group_key: source human text; polished variants linked by 5-gram Jaccard, unlinked variants kept as singletons
corpora.use: Polish sensitivity: which rules appear after AI polishing of human drafts (Task 4 introduced_by_polish); development set in Task 7.

corpora.licence: Public research download; reuse terms unconfirmed. Confirm before any redistribution. Never committed.
corpora.group_key: session (writer grouping not implemented: metadata workbook not parsed)
corpora.use: Provenance research: reconstructed final text per session, for the guard and any later event-level analysis. No performance measure is planned.

corpora.licence: U.S. Government Publishing Office collection. Confirm reuse terms before redistribution. Never committed.
corpora.use: Pre-LLM civic human control (Task 3 comparison c); held-out human controls in Task 7 after exclusion from Tasks 3-6.
